tools.name: health
tools.description: Database freshness: CVE/KEV/CWE counts and latest entries, and the sync state of each upstream feed. last_synced is when a feed's state was last written; read it with last_status. Costs no credits.

tools.name: cve_lookup
tools.description: Full CVE record by ID (CVSS, EPSS, KEV, CWE, references, CISA SSVC, Nuclei templates), with the optional GitHub Security Advisory. Call the cve_products tool for every affected product. Unknown impact? Read ssvc.mission_wellbeing.high.

tools.name: cve_lookup_bulk
tools.description: Look up many CVEs at once, each with the fields of cve_lookup. Ids beyond the remaining credits come back in not_processed. Costs 1 credit per CVE ID looked up, at least 1.

tools.name: cve_products
tools.description: The products a CVE affects, one page at a time, with the vulnerable products first. The vendor and product arguments keep only the products with that exact name. For the CVEs of one product, call cve_search.

tools.name: cve_search
tools.description: Search CVEs by severity, CWE, CVSS, EPSS, CISA KEV, ransomware use, Nuclei template, vendor, product and publish date, one page at a time. Call the cve_lookup tool for a full record, and the cpe_search tool to find the names.

tools.name: cve_leading
tools.description: List the CVEs most likely to be exploited, by EPSS score (the probability of exploitation in the next 30 days), with a verdict on the top score. To rank by composite risk score, call the cve_triage tool.

tools.name: kev_lookup
tools.description: CISA KEV entry of a CVE: required action, patch deadline, ransomware use. A removed CVE gives in_kev false, a never-listed one the tool error "KEV entry not found". Full CVE record: cve_lookup. CVEs in KEV now: cve_search with in_kev=true.

tools.name: cwe_lookup
tools.description: CWE weakness details (description, mitigations, examples, OWASP Top 10 category in 2021 and 2025), with how many CVEs and CISA KEV entries name it. To list them, call the cve_search tool with its cwe_id argument.

tools.name: cve_risk_score
tools.description: Composite risk score of a CVE, 0-100, for patch priority. It reads EPSS, CISA KEV, Metasploit, CVSS, NVD and CNA exploit references, and ExploitDB. has_public_poc is null when no source names an exploit. For many CVEs, call cve_triage_bulk.

tools.name: cve_exploit
tools.description: Public exploit intelligence (GitHub PoCs, Metasploit, NVD and CNA exploit references, ExploitDB). GitHub PoC repositories are listed but not counted as proof of a public exploit. For a single patch-priority score, call cve_risk_score.

tools.name: cve_triage
tools.description: Rank the CVEs of a vendor or product by composite risk score, at or above the optional min_risk_score argument, as lean rows (cve_id, risk_score, label). Call the cve_lookup tool for detail, and the cpe_search tool to find the names.

tools.name: epss_risers
tools.description: List the CVEs whose EPSS score rose most over the last 7 or 30 days, with the old and the new score. Filter by vendor, product, KEV state or a minimum score. Call the cve_lookup tool for the details of a CVE.

tools.name: cve_triage_bulk
tools.description: Triage many CVEs at once, ranked by composite risk score. Ids beyond the remaining credits come back in not_processed. Costs 1 credit per CVE ID triaged, at least 1.

tools.name: product_exposure
tools.description: CVE exposure of one vendor and product: severity, KEV and PoC counts, CVSS, EPSS, the worst risk score, the top CVEs and the endoflife.date support dates. To find the names, call the cpe_search tool.

tools.name: cpe_search
tools.description: Find the CPE vendor and product names that hold a text, ranked by vulnerable CVE count. Pass a name with no % as it is to the vendor and product arguments of the cve_search, cve_triage, cve_leading, product_exposure and epss_risers tools.

tools.name: cvss_calculator
tools.description: Decode a CVSS v3.0/v3.1 vector into its base metrics and recompute its base, temporal and environmental scores. Use it on a vector you hold; cve_lookup already gives the scores of a CVE. v2 and v4 are refused.

tools.name: watchlist_edit
tools.description: Add, remove, list or clear the items this API key watches: CVEs, products, CVE searches, packages, domains and IP addresses. Read their changes with the watchlist_events tool. Requires a Pro API key.

tools.name: watchlist_events
tools.description: Report what changed on the items this API key watches, such as a new advisory for a package or a certificate about to expire, oldest first. A plain call continues where the last one stopped. Requires a Pro API key.

tools.name: privacy_my_data
tools.description: What this server keeps about the caller: the hash its credits are counted under, the rate limit left in this hour and the privacy policy. For a Pro key, which vendor keys are stored and a 15-minute link to change them.

tools.name: vendor_key_edit
tools.description: Save, delete or check your own Shodan and AbuseIPDB keys, which the ip_lookup tool uses. Needs a Pro API key or a manage link. The privacy_my_data tool gives a web link where a person can save the keys without the agent seeing them.

tools.name: password_check
tools.description: Check a password's SHA-1 against Have I Been Pwned's Pwned Passwords list. It takes the full SHA-1, never the password. Only its first 5 hex digits leave this server.

tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Look up a domain's DNS records: A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, CNAME, SOA and CAA. A record type the resolver could not answer is listed under unavailable.

tools.name: dns_takeover_check
tools.description: Check a host name for subdomain takeover through a dangling CNAME. takeover_possible is null when the CNAME points to a service whose DNS does not show whether the name can be claimed.

tools.name: email_auth_check
tools.description: Check a domain's mail authentication: SPF, DMARC (from a parent domain when the domain has no record of its own), DKIM, MX and MTA-STS, each check with pass, warn or fail and a severity.

tools.name: email_address_check
tools.description: Check an e-mail address without sending mail: whether its domain exists and takes mail, and whether a disposable domain list names it. It cannot tell whether the mailbox exists.

tools.name: ssl_check
tools.description: Check the TLS certificate and settings of a host name on port 443: version, cipher, trust, OCSP revocation, expiry, DNS names, the chain and an abuse.ch SSL Blacklist listing.

tools.name: headers_check
tools.description: Rate nine security headers of a web site, such as CSP, HSTS and Set-Cookie, from one GET to https://<domain>/ that follows up to 5 redirects on the same host or its www pair. Each finding that does not pass has a remediation.

tools.name: well_known
tools.description: Read robots.txt of https://<domain> and, if it allows us, /.well-known/security.txt, with up to 5 redirects on the host or its www pair. Gives the rules that bind us, sitemaps, fields such as Contact and Expires, and RFC 9309/9116 issues.

tools.name: redirect_chain
tools.description: Follow an http or https URL's redirects, up to 10 requests on ports 80 and 443. Lists each hop and status, the final URL, the stop reason and any https to http step. Reads no body; no HTML or JavaScript redirect. Location text is untrusted.

tools.name: whois_lookup
tools.description: Look up a domain's registration over RDAP, or WHOIS where allowed: registrar, dates, status, name servers and DNSSEC. A name under a registered domain asks about that domain. No registrant data.

tools.name: wayback_lookup
tools.description: List when the Wayback Machine captured a host's home page: the first and last capture, the years between them (archive span, not domain age) and the latest 10 captures with links.

tools.name: cert_search
tools.description: List the unexpired certificates that Certificate Transparency logs hold for a host name, wildcards included, from SSLMate's Cert Spotter: the 10 newest, with issuer, validity and DNS names. Costs 2 credits.

tools.name: subdomain_enum
tools.description: List up to 50 subdomains of a registrable domain from Certificate Transparency, DNS queries for 94 common names and the domain's MX, NS and SPF records, and, when DNS can tell, whether each listed name has an IPv4 address. Costs 2 credits.

tools.name: ip_lookup
tools.description: Look up a public IP: AS, country, cloud provider, CDN, datacenter, Tor exit, crawler, DROP listing and PTR name. A Pro key with its own Shodan or AbuseIPDB key adds exposure and reputation. For every prefix of the AS, call asn_lookup.

tools.name: asn_lookup
tools.description: Look up an autonomous system by number, such as AS15169, or by an IP address it holds: name, country and one page of its IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes, derived from IPtoASN.

tools.name: d3fend_for_attack
tools.description: MITRE D3FEND defenses that counter a MITRE ATT&CK technique. A technique id such as T1055 also matches its sub-techniques. Source: MITRE D3FEND (MIT license).

tools.name: driver_lookup
tools.description: Look up a Windows driver hash in the LOLDrivers catalog of vulnerable and malicious drivers. Block on the file and Authenticode hashes, not on the detection rules. For many hashes, call driver_lookup_bulk. Source: LOLDrivers (Apache-2.0).

tools.name: driver_lookup_bulk
tools.description: Look up many driver file hashes in the LOLDrivers catalog at once, each with the fields of driver_lookup. Hashes beyond the remaining credits come back in not_processed. Costs 1 credit per hash looked up, at least 1.

tools.name: package_check
tools.description: Check a package against the OSV.dev advisories (GitHub, Go, PyPA, RustSec) and the OpenSSF malicious package list, with the fixed version and endoflife.date dates. For severity, pass the CVE aliases to the cve_triage_bulk tool.

tools.name: package_check_bulk
tools.description: Check many packages at once, each an ecosystem, a name and an exact version, against the advisories package_check reads. For the summary and ranges of an advisory, call the package_check tool. Costs 1 credit per package checked, at least 1.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: health, email_auth_check, email_address_check, well_known · Private data: health, cve_lookup, cve_search, kev_lookup, watchlist_edit, watchlist_events, vendor_key_edit, password_check, dns_lookup, email_auth_check, well_known, subdomain_enum, driver_lookup, driver_lookup_bulk · Public sink: cve_search, email_auth_check, email_address_check · Destructive: watchlist_edit, vendor_key_edit, ip_lookup.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: health, email_auth_check, email_address_check, well_known · Private data: health, cve_lookup, cve_search, kev_lookup, watchlist_edit, watchlist_events, vendor_key_edit, password_check, dns_lookup, email_auth_check, well_known, subdomain_enum, driver_lookup, driver_lookup_bulk · Public sink: cve_search, email_auth_check, email_address_check · Destructive: watchlist_edit, vendor_key_edit, ip_lookup

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
